chapter_title_en: Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved
chapter_expert_explanation_en: One of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
აწ საყვარელსა მიუწერს გულ-ამოსკვნილი მტირალი
მისმანვე ცრემლმან დაუვსის ვის ედებოდა ვის ალი!
დაწერა წიგნი, მსმენელთა გულისა გასაგმირალი,
და ვარდი გააპის, გამოჩნდის მუნ ბროლი გამომჭვირვალი
stanzas.english_translation: "Now will I, sobbing, weeping, write to my beloved; by the tear of that one who burns him is a man's fire quenched." She wrote a letter piercing the heart of the hearers. She splits the rose (opens her mouth); there appears the translucent crystal.

stanzas.english_translation: "O mine own! this letter is the work of my hands; for pen I have my form, a pen steeped in gall; for paper I glue thy heart even to my heart; O heart, black (sad) heart, thou art bound, loose not thyself, now be bounds!

“ჰხედავცა, ჩემო, სოფელი რათა საქმეთა მქმნელია!
რაზომცა ნათობს სინათლე, ჩემთვის ეგრეცა ბნელია.

stanzas.english_translation: "Thou seest, O mine own! of what deeds the world is a doer. However much light shines, for me it is but darkness. The wise know it (the world), therefore they despise it, to them it is contemptible. My life without thee, woe is me! how exceeding hard it is!

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ჰხედავ, ჩემო, ვით გაგვყარნა სოფელმან და ჟამმან კრულმან,

stanzas.english_translation: "Thou seest, mine own! how Fate and cursed time have parted us; no longer do I glad see thee, my glad loved one; what, indeed, can the heart rent by thee do without thee! Secret thought manifests to thee what is hidden (?).

stanzas.english_translation: "By thy sun (life)! until now I thought not thou wert alive; as for me, methought my life and all my resource had passed away. Now when I hear (news of thee), I magnify the Creator and humble myself before God. All mine erstwhile grief I weigh as joy.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 51 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 1296; Wardrop Stanza 1273): Part of the narrative sequence in which one of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“შენი სიცოცხლე მეყოფის ჩემად იმედად გულისად,
გულისა ერთობ წყლულისა და ასრე დადაგულისად.

stanzas.english_translation: "Thy life is sufficient for my heart to hope in, a heart all wounded and so consumed! Think of me, remember me as one lost to thee; I sit nursing the love I planted.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 51 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 1297; Wardrop Stanza 1274): Part of the narrative sequence in which one of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

“სხვად, ჩემო, ჩემი ამბავი ჩემგან არ მოგეწერების:
ენა დაშვრების, მოსმენით არვისგან დაიჯერების.
ფატმან წამგვარა გრძნეულთა, ღმერთიმცა მას ეტერების,
და აწ კვლა ქმნა იგი სოფელმან, რაცა მას შეეფერების.
stanzas.english_translation: "Now, O mine own, my story is not to be written to thee by me; the tongue will tire, none that hear will believe! P’hatman took me from sorcerers; may God protect her! Now again Fate hath done what befits it.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 51 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 1298; Wardrop Stanza 1275): Part of the narrative sequence in which one of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

“აწ სოფელმან უარესი ჭირი ჭირსა მომისართა,
არ დასჯერდა ბედი ჩემი მას პატიჟთა მრავალ-გვართა;

stanzas.english_translation: "Fate hath now added worse woe to my woe, my ill luck was not appeased by these manifold afflictions; and again it delivered me into the hands of the Kadjis, hard to combat; Fate hath done to us, mine own, all that hath befallen us.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 51 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 1299; Wardrop Stanza 1276): Part of the narrative sequence in which one of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

“ციხეს ვზი ეზომ მაღალსა, თვალნი ძლივ გარდასწვდებიან,
გზა გვირაბითა შემოვა, მცველნი მუნ ზედა დგებიან,
დღისით და ღამით მოყმენი ნობათსა არ დასცდებიან,

stanzas.english_translation: "I am sitting in a castle so lofty that eyes can scarce see the ground; the road enters by a passage, over it stand guards; day and night knights miss not their turn as sentries, they will kill those that engage them, like fire will they envelop them.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 51 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 1300; Wardrop Stanza 1277): Part of the narrative sequence in which one of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

stanzas.english_translation: "Surely thou thinkest not that these are of the same kind as other warriors? Slay me not with woes worse than the present! I shall see thee dead, I shall be burnt up like tinder by steel. (Since) I am sundered from thee, renounce me with a heart harder than rock itself. 1278a" Beloved, sorrow not with such grief! Tell me, can there be for me another with the form of an aloe-tree! Life without thee is nought for me, henceforth I should be full of regret; either I would cast myself down from the rock or slay myself with a knife.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 51 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 1301; Wardrop Stanza 1278): Part of the narrative sequence in which one of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

stanzas.english_translation: "By thy sun (life)! thy moon 1 will fall to the lot of none save thee! By thy sun! to none shall she fall though triple suns shone forth! Here would I dash myself down; the great rocks are very nigh to me. To thee would I commit my soul; perchance wings would be given to me by Heaven.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 51 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 1302; Wardrop Stanza 1279): Part of the narrative sequence in which one of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“შენმან მზემან, უშენოსა არვის მიჰხვდეს მთვარე შენი,
შენმან მზემან ვერვის მიჰხვდეს, მოცავიდენ სამნი მზენი;
აქა თავსა გარდავიქცევ, ახლოს მახლვან დიდნი კლდენი,
და სული ჩემი შეივედრე, ზეცით მომხვდენ ნუთუ ფრთენი.
stanzas.english_translation: "Entreat God for me; it may be He will deliver me from the travail of the world and from union with fire, water, earth and air. Let Him give me wings and I shall fly up, I shall attain my desire--day and night I shall gaze on the sun's rays flashing in splendour.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 51 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 1303; Wardrop Stanza 1280): Part of the narrative sequence in which one of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ღმერთსა შემვედრე, ნუთუ კვლა დამხსნა სოფლისა შრომასა,
ცეცხლსა, წყალსა და მიწასა, ჰაერთა თანა ძრომასა;

და დღისით და ღამით ვჰხედვიდე მზისა ელვათა კრთომასა.
stanzas.english_translation: "The sun cannot be without thee, for thou art an atom of it; of a surety thou shalt adhere to it as its zodiac (Leo), and not as one rejected. There shall I see thee; I shall liken thee to it, thou shalt enlighten my darkened heart. If my life was bitter, let my death be sweet!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 51 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 1304; Wardrop Stanza 1281): Part of the narrative sequence in which one of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

“მზე უშენოდ ვერ იქმნების, რათგან შენ ხარ მისი წილი,
განაღამცა მას იახელ მისი ეტლი, არ თუ წბილი!
მუნა გნახო, მანდვე გსახო, განმინათლო გული ჩრდილი,

stanzas.english_translation: "Death is no longer grievous to me, since it is to thee I commit my soul; but I have laid thy love in my heart, and there it rests. When I think of parting from thee, for me wound is added to wound. Weep not and mourn not for me, O mine own, for love of me!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 51 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 1305; Wardrop Stanza 1282): Part of the narrative sequence in which one of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

stanzas.english_translation: "Go, betake thyself to India, be of some help to my father, who is straitened by foes, helpless on all sides; comfort the heart of him who suffers separation from me. Think of me weeping for thy sake with undrying tears.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 51 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 1306; Wardrop Stanza 1283): Part of the narrative sequence in which one of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“წადი, ინდოეთს მიმართე, არგე რა ჩემსა მშობელსა,
მტერთაგან შეიწრებულსა, ყოვლგნით ხელ-აღუპყრობელსა,

და მომიგონებდი მტირალსა, შენთვის ცრემლ-შეუშრობელსა.
stanzas.english_translation: "Whatever complaint I have made against my Fate is sufficient complaint. Know this, that true justice goeth from heart to heart; for thy sake will I die, I shall become the prey of ravens! But as long as I live I shall weep and suffer enough for thee, too.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 51 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 1307; Wardrop Stanza 1284): Part of the narrative sequence in which one of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“რაცა ვიჩივლე ბედისა ჩემისა, კმა საჩივარად;
ცან, სამართალი მართალი გულისა გულსა მივა რად.
შენთვის მოვკვდები, გავხდები ყორანთა დასაყივარად,

stanzas.english_translation: "Lo, mark the token from the veil that was thine; from one end I have cut off a strip, O mine own; this (the veil) is all that is left to me in place of that great hope; in wrath the wheels of the seven heavens has turned upon us."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 51 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 1308; Wardrop Stanza 1285): Part of the narrative sequence in which one of the lyrical masterpieces of Georgian literature (Stanzas 1292–1317): Nestan-Darejan writes to Tariel expressing her undying love, sending a fringe cut from the Khatavian veil he gave her, warning him not to rush into certain death at Kadjeti, and uttering her famous prayer of spiritual transcendence ('Entrust me to God, perchance He will free me from the travail of the world... grant me wings that I may fly', Stanza 1304).

“აჰა, ინიშნე ნიშანი შენეულისა რიდისა,
გარდმიკვეთია ალამი, ჩემო, ერთისა კიდისა,

stanzas.english_translation: When she had finished this letter written to her beloved, she cut off a fringe from those veils; bareheaded, the thick, long locks of her hair became her well, the scent blows from the aloe, breathing through the raven's wings.

ესე წიგნი, საყვარელსა მისსა თანა მინაწერი,

stanzas.english_translation: That slave departed, journeying to Gulansharo; in one instant he reached P’hatman's, he travelled not many days. When this matter so dear to him had been accomplished, Avt’handil with hands upraised thanks God, with full understanding, not as one bemused.
